title: Normalized algebraic duality: degree bounds and depth detection for a finite module

source.place: Tag 0A7U (lemma-sitting-in-degrees), parts (1) and (3), for nonzero finite modules (proved together by the induction on dim Supp(M) in its proof); the zero module is excluded because its depth is infinite; dualizing complex as in Tag 0A7B (definition-dualizing), normalized as in the opening paragraph of section-dualizing-local, stated inline.

proof.text: Write $D^i(T)=H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(T[0],K)$ for any finite $T$. The hypotheses on $K$ are used as written inline, without a separate dualizing-definition node. By [lem-trf-coherent-rhom-finite-injective-dimension], applied with source $T[0]$ and target $K$, every $D^i(T)$ is finite. For nonzero finite $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-depth-ext] gives finite depth. Also $\operatorname{Ann}_A(T)$ is proper and contained in $\mathfrak m$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] puts $\mathfrak m$ in its support. Every prime chain of its support is a prime chain of $A$; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] therefore gives $0\le d_T\le\dim A<\infty$. We have $D^i(0)=0$, directly from the zero Hom complex.

Fix a bounded injective representative $J$ of $K$. The natural derived isomorphism of [lem-trf-bounded-injective-rhom-model-support], applied to $T[0]$, computes $D^i(T)$ as $H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(T[0],J)$. For $0\to U\to V\to W\to0$, apply [lem-trf-bounded-injective-total-hom-exact] to the complexes in degree zero, then [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. This gives $\cdots\to D^i(W)\to D^i(V)\to D^i(U)\to D^{i+1}(W)\to\cdots$. The naturality clause of the model node identifies these arrows with the maps induced by the given module maps. If $U\to V$ is multiplication by $f$ on $T$, its Hom-complex map is multiplication by $f$, since $\varphi(ft)=f\varphi(t)$ termwise; its cohomology map is consequently multiplication by $f$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0A7U (lemma-sitting-in-degrees), long exact sequences in the proof; Tag 0G4H, bounded injective computation; homology.tex Tag 0117.

proof.text: For a finite-length $A$-module $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-length-module-simple-filtration] gives $0=L_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq L_r=L$ with simple factors. Each simple factor $S$ is $\kappa$: if $0\ne z\in S$, simplicity makes $a\mapsto az$ a surjection $A\to S$ with proper kernel $I$; a strict intermediate ideal $I\subsetneq J\subsetneq A$ would give a proper nonzero submodule of $S$. Thus $I$ is maximal, hence $I=\mathfrak m$. These maps identify all factors with $\kappa$. In particular $\mathfrak m L_j\subseteq L_{j-1}$, so $\mathfrak m^r L=0$; if $L\ne0$ then $r\ge1$ and $L_1\cong\kappa$ embeds in $L$.

source.place: Tag 0A7U, dimension-zero case, and lemma-dualizing-finite-length, opening length induction; algebra.tex Tag 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces), parts (2),(3).

source.place: Tag 0A7U, dimension-zero case; lemma-dualizing-finite-length, first sentence of its proof.

proof.text: We now prove by strong induction on $d\ge0$ that every nonzero finite $T$ with $d_T=d$ satisfies $D^i(T)=0$ for $i<-d$ or $i>0$. When $d=0$, any prime of its support distinct from $\mathfrak m$ would give a strict length-one chain ending in $\mathfrak m$, which belongs to the support by Step 1. Hence its support is $\{\mathfrak m\}$. By [lem-sc-generic-stalk-finite-length], $T$ has finite length. Step 4 gives exactly the desired vanishing. For $d>0$ assume the bounds for every nonzero finite module of support dimension strictly below $d$; first prove the positive-depth case at dimension $d$, then the depth-zero case.

source.place: Tag 0A7U (lemma-sitting-in-degrees), induction on support dimension; algebra.tex Tag 00L5 (lemma-support-point).

proof.text: Suppose $d_T=d>0$ and $\operatorname{depth}(T)>0$. The supremum definition of depth gives a regular sequence of positive length; its first element $f\in\mathfrak m$ acts injectively on $T$. Put $Q=T/fT$. Its finite generating set is given by the images of generators of $T$, and $Q\ne0$ by Nakayama. The nonzerodivisor clause of [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-equality] gives $d_Q+1=d_T$, so $d_Q=d-1$. The dimension induction in Step 5 applies to $Q$ and gives $D^j(Q)=0$ for $j<-(d-1)$ or $j>0$. Step 2 applies to $0\to T\xrightarrow{f}T\to Q\to0$.

source.place: Tag 0A7U, positive-depth dimension induction; algebra.tex Tag 0B52 (lemma-one-equation-module), nonzerodivisor clause; Tags 00LI, 00LF, 00DV.

proof.text: For $i<-d$ we have $i+1<-(d-1)$, and for $i>0$ we have $i+1>0$. Thus $D^{i+1}(Q)=0$ in either case by Step 6. The exact segment $D^i(T)\xrightarrow f D^i(T)\to D^{i+1}(Q)$ gives $fD^i(T)=D^i(T)$. The module $D^i(T)$ is finite by Step 1; the ideal $(f)$ is contained in the Jacobson radical $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson], $D^i(T)=0$. This establishes the bounds for all positive-depth modules of dimension $d$ before any depth-zero module of dimension $d$ is considered.

source.place: Tag 0A7U, positive-depth dimension induction and Nakayama; algebra.tex Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK).

proof.text: For $d_T=d>0$ with depth zero, set $N=T[\mathfrak m^\infty]=\{z\in T:\mathfrak m^e z=0\text{ for some }e\ge1\}$ and $T'=T/N$. The set $N$ is a submodule: a maximum of two annihilating exponents works for a sum, and scalar multiplication preserves the condition. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], $N$ is finite. Choose finitely many generators and take the maximum $e$ of their annihilating exponents, obtaining $\mathfrak m^e N=0$ (take $e=1$ if $N=0$). At any prime $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m$, choose $a\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak q$; then $a^eN=0$, and $a$ acts invertibly after localization, so $N_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Hence, if $N\ne0$, [lem-sc-generic-stalk-finite-length] gives it finite length, and Step 4 applies. If $N=0$ its dual vanishes by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0A7U, depth-zero reduction to maximal-ideal power torsion; algebra.tex Tags 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), 00L5 (lemma-support-point).

For $\mathfrak q
e\mathfrak m$, the quotient map gives an isomorphism $T_{\mathfrak q}	o T'_{\mathfrak q}$, directly on fractions: it is surjective by lifting numerators, and if $z/s$ maps to zero, some $u
otin\mathfrak q$ has $uz\in N$, whence $a^euz=0$ for the $a$ of Step 8, so $z/s=0$. Since $d>0$, the support of $T$ contains a prime other than $\mathfrak m$; thus $T'
e0$. It is finite as a quotient. Step 1 puts $\mathfrak m$ in both supports. The fraction isomorphisms identify their remaining support points, so $\operatorname{Supp}(T')=\operatorname{Supp}(T)$ and $d_{T'}=d$. This argument uses only the fraction equality and zero criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Tag 0A7U, depth-zero paragraph: dim Supp(M/N)=d; direct fraction verification of the support identification.

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-by-power-torsion-no-torsion], $T'[\mathfrak m]=0$. In particular no element of $T'$ has annihilator exactly $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] there is an $f\in\mathfrak m$ acting injectively on $T'$. Nakayama makes $T'/fT'$ nonzero, so the depth and regular-sequence definitions give $\operatorname{depth}(T')>0$. Steps 6--7, already proved for positive depth at dimension $d$, give the bounds for $T'$. Step 2 applied to $0\to N\to T\to T'\to0$ has segment $D^i(T')\to D^i(T)\to D^i(N)$. For $i<-d$ or $i>0$, the first term is zero by those bounds and the last is zero by Step 4, since $i\ne0$. Thus $D^i(T)=0$. This finishes the dimension induction and proves clause (1), without a pre-existing dualizing-bounds theorem.

source.place: Tag 0A7U, depth-zero paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 05EB (lemma-divide-by-torsion), part (1); algebra.tex Tags 00LL, 00DV, 00LI, 00LF.

proof.text:
We prove by induction on $n\ge0$ that for every nonzero finite $T$ of depth $n$, $D^{-n}(T)
e0$ and $D^i(T)=0$ for $i>-n$. For $n=0$, no $f\in\mathfrak m$ can be injective on $T$: Nakayama applied to $(f)$ makes $T/fT$ nonzero, so such an $f$ would be a regular sequence of length one, contradicting the definition of depth. The contrapositive of [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] supplies $z\in T$ with annihilator exactly $\mathfrak m$. (Such $z$ is nonzero because the annihilator of zero is $A$.) Thus $a mod\mathfrak m\mapsto az$ embeds $\kappa$ into $T$. Set $W=T/Az$, a finite quotient. Step 2 gives $D^0(T)	o D^0(\kappa)	o D^1(W)$. Step 10 gives $D^1(W)=0$ when $W
e0$, and Step 1 covers $W=0$, and normalization gives $D^0(\kappa)\cong\kappa
e0$. The surjection onto this nonzero module proves $D^0(T)
e0$. Step 10 supplies the required vanishing for $i>0$.

source.place: Tag 0A7U (lemma-sitting-in-degrees), depth-zero case, with its socle argument written directly; algebra.tex Tags 00LL (lemma-ideal-nonzerodivisor), 00DV (lemma-NAK), 00LI (definition-depth), 00LF (definition-regular-sequence).

proof.text: Let $n>0$ and assume the induction claim for all nonzero finite modules of depth $n-1$. If $T$ has depth $n$, the supremum defining depth contains a regular sequence of positive length; otherwise its only possible length would be zero. Its first element $f\in\mathfrak m$ is injective on $T$. Put $Q=T/fT$. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one], $Q\ne0$ and has depth $n-1$; it is finite since the images of any finite generating set of $T$ generate $Q$. The induction hypothesis therefore gives $D^{-(n-1)}(Q)\ne0$ and $D^j(Q)=0$ for every $j>-(n-1)$. The short exact sequence $0\to T\xrightarrow{f}T\to Q\to0$ satisfies the hypotheses of Step 2.

For any integer $i>-n$, we have $i+1>-(n-1)$, so $D^{i+1}(Q)=0$ by Step 12. Exactness of $D^i(T)\xrightarrow{f}D^i(T)\to D^{i+1}(Q)$ from Step 2 gives $fD^i(T)=D^i(T)$. The module $D^i(T)$ is finite by Step 1, and $(f)$ lies in the Jacobson radical since $A$ is local and $f\in\mathfrak m$. Nakayama therefore gives $D^i(T)=0$. This proves the vanishing half of the induction claim in all degrees $i>-n$.
